cases.title: Initiate drag event and capture product title and price
cases.description: Drag a product item 'li' element with draggable='true' and verify that the drag event initiates and successfully captures the product's title and price for transfer.

cases.title: Drop product item into drop area to add to cart
cases.description: Verify that dragging and dropping a product item (e.g., data-testid='product-item-1') into the designated drop area (id='div1', data-testid='drop-area') adds it to the cart and automatically updates the cart display: product title in .box2, unit price in .box3, and quantity in .box1.

cases.title: Add repeated products to the cart
cases.description: Verify that dropping the same product item multiple times into the designated drop area correctly updates and accumulates the quantity and information in the cart display.

cases.title: Calculate and display total price formatted in the allMoney element
cases.description: Verify that the system calculates the total price by summing the prices of all products in the cart, formats the total to two decimal places with the appropriate currency symbol, and displays it in the div id="allMoney" element.

opinions.feedback: All requirements are properly covered by the test cases, and there are no blockers or missing scenarios.

analysis.analysis: Requirement e2edev_bench_01-R-1 describes multiple distinct behaviors including initiating a drag event, capturing the product title, and capturing the product price, with normal paths for dragging draggable 'li' elements. Requirement e2edev_bench_01-R-3 specifies behaviors for dropping items into a designated drop area, updating the cart display elements (.box1, .box2, .box3) with quantity, title, and unit price, and supporting both different and repeated products. Requirement e2edev_bench_01-R-5 defines the calculation of the total price by summing product prices, formatting to two decimal places with a currency symbol, and displaying the result in the <div id="allMoney"> element. None of the requirements explicitly mention error conditions, abnormal paths, or specific boundary parameters beyond the normal execution of these stated behaviors.
